## Issue tracking

For PRs from open-source community contributors:

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: <!-- e.g. Fixes #1234 / Related to #1234 -->

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [ ] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

### Keep the profiling baseline nondeterministic

With the new default, the existing [performance harness](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f24fc209b539fc6711771f5d5011a5b3f2fe8fb3/tests/performance_tests/shell_test_utils/determinism/perf_breakdown.sh#L18-L63) now launches **both** arms deterministically: its `det` arm passes the deprecated positive flag, while its `nondet` arm passes no determinism flag. Both therefore enter this branch. The [runner](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f24fc209b539fc6711771f5d5011a5b3f2fe8fb3/tests/performance_tests/shell_test_utils/determinism/run_nsys_breakdown.sh#L13-L22) still labels their profiles det/nondet, and the [ratio check](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f24fc209b539fc6711771f5d5011a5b3f2fe8fb3/tests/performance_tests/shell_test_utils/determinism/print_nsys_leaderboard.py#L98-L110) consequently compares det against det instead of detecting determinism overhead.

Replace line 58 of the harness with:

```bash
        $([ "$DETERMINISM_PERF_MODE" = nondet ] && echo --disable-deterministic-mode) \
```

This retains the intended default-on production behavior and the deterministic arm, while restoring an explicitly opted-out baseline. Keep the existing mode names, log directories, profiling arguments and ratio calculation unchanged.

Proposed acceptance: capture argv for both harness launches and assert that only `nondet` contains `--disable-deterministic-mode`. In fresh processes, the det launch must enable the helper/model determinism and pass `deterministic=True` to tuning installation; nondet must skip the helper, produce a false model flag and pass `deterministic=False`. Re-run the profiling recipe to verify that both profiles and the comparison still complete. This failure and replacement are source-reasoned, not executed.

Static light review; tests were not executed. The performance comparison regression is noted inline. Two additional fixes are needed below. Suggested code must be verified before adoption.

### Add regression tests for the new CLI polarity and compatibility behavior

The functional recipe migrations exercise ordinary launches, but do not explicitly assert the new destination/inversion or the precedence of the deprecated flag. The existing [determinism argument tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f24fc209b539fc6711771f5d5011a5b3f2fe8fb3/tests/unit_tests/training/test_determinism_args.py#L33-L69) call the helper directly, while [the initialization test](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f24fc209b539fc6711771f5d5011a5b3f2fe8fb3/tests/unit_tests/tuning/test_autotune_config.py#L128-L141) only checks the legacy positive flag. Neither pins down the new opt-out contract.

Add this focused parser-to-config regression beside the existing [adapter tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f24fc209b539fc6711771f5d5011a5b3f2fe8fb3/tests/unit_tests/test_argument_utils.py#L84-L99), using their existing imports and capturing config:

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "flags, expected",
    [
        ([], True),
        (["--deterministic-mode"], True),
        (["--disable-deterministic-mode"], False),
        (["--deterministic-mode", "--disable-deterministic-mode"], False),
        (["--disable-deterministic-mode", "--deterministic-mode"], False),
    ],
)
def test_cli_determinism_reaches_transformer_config(flags, expected):
    parser = add_megatron_arguments(ArgumentParser())
    args = parser.parse_args(flags)
    args.params_dtype = torch.float32
    config = core_transformer_config_from_args(
        args, config_class=CapturingTransformerConfig
    )
    assert args.disable_deterministic_mode == (not expected)
    assert config.deterministic_mode is expected
```

Required companion checks: parameterize the existing initialization test with the same cases and assert `tuning.install(..., deterministic=expected)`; with minimal valid training arguments and a mocked determinism helper, assert that `validate_args` calls it only when `expected` is true. This preserves default-on CLI behavior, opt-out precedence in either flag order, and the legacy flag warning without making it an opt-in again. Also retain the separate library contract: directly constructing `TransformerConfig(num_layers=1, hidden_size=128, num_attention_heads=4)` must still yield `deterministic_mode=False`. These are proposed checks, not executed results.

### Update the deterministic-training guide for the default change

The affected [user guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f24fc209b539fc6711771f5d5011a5b3f2fe8fb3/docs/user-guide/deterministic-training.md#L14-L22) still instructs users to opt in with `--deterministic-mode` and never documents the opt-out. After this PR, merely omitting that old flag does not disable determinism—for example, a training launch with `--tp-comm-overlap` still reaches the deterministic guard.

Replace the opening opt-in instructions/example with text such as:

> Deterministic mode is enabled by default for Megatron's argparse CLI. Pass `--disable-deterministic-mode` to opt out. The legacy `--deterministic-mode` flag is deprecated and ignored; it does not override the opt-out. Directly constructed Python configuration dataclasses retain their `deterministic_mode=False` default.

Update the flag-labeled explanations in the configuration table and Triton section to describe the enabled mode rather than imply opt-in. Preserve the documented environment restrictions, incompatible-option checks, and kernel-selection behavior; those still apply when determinism is enabled. Static acceptance: the guide must explicitly distinguish CLI and dataclass defaults, document the opt-out and legacy precedence, and no longer present the deprecated flag as necessary to enable determinism.
